chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Hariz, from Walid, who said:

A questioning woman came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Mothers, kind and merciful to their children, if it were not for what they do that comes to their husbands, it would be said to them: Enter Paradise without reckoning.'

key_terms.سَائِلَةٌ: A woman who came to ask a question

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for mothers entering Paradise without reckoning according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the immense spiritual status of mothers, attributing to them the qualities of 'Wali dat' (deities/goddesses of mercy) due to their profound compassion for their offspring. The Prophet (peace be upon him) notes that their entry into Paradise would be without reckoning (bi-ghayr hisab) were it not for the specific marital duties they owe to their husbands, illustrating the balance between maternal mercy and conjugal rights in Shia jurisprudence. This narration underscores the high value placed on motherhood while simultaneously affirming the structural integrity of the family unit through the wife's obligation to her spouse.
